doc.title: Art Farmer — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Meeting Gil Evans and Hal McKusick on record dates
summary: Gil Evans arranged on dates with Teddy Charles and McKusick, before Miles recorded similar pieces.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Cannonball Adderley: the sound, the man, the band

blocks.x: Was Hal McKusick in that band?
No, he wasn’t in that band. I met Hal through the dates with Gil Evans and Teddy Charles.
We didn’t talk about the dates with Gil Evans.

Gil was the one who was writing the music on either Teddy Charles’ date or Hal McKusick’s date, and Gil wrote the arrangements. That’s when I first met Gil. I think I made maybe one or two other albums with him of the same type. In fact, some of the tunes that he arranged for Miles to play, we had already done them. That was the start of a certain sound. Hal was and is a very good alto player. We just played a date together about two months ago out on Long Island. I can’t remember the name of the place where we were.
